$comment: Pinned external dependencies for Rebuild Studio on Windows. Consumed by scripts/windows/Setup-Dependencies.ps1 and Doctor-RebuildStudio.ps1. An artifact with sha256 == null is NEVER installed (verify_required). Compute with: Setup-Dependencies.ps1 -ComputeHash <tool>, review the source, then paste the value here.

rizin.role: Native analysis engine with the rz-ghidra decompiler (subprocess via rzpipe; never linked). Windows artifact is the official Cutter v2.5.0 build, which bundles rizin at the same commit as rizin v0.9.1 plus rz-ghidra; the plain rizin Windows release has no decompiler plugin.
rizin.license: LGPL-3.0-only (rizin), LGPL-3.0 (rz-ghidra), Apache-2.0 (Ghidra decompiler), GPL-3.0 (Cutter GUI files in the archive; not used)

artifact.name: Cutter-v2.5.0-Windows-x86_64.zip
artifact.hash_provenance: 2026-10-06 on Windows 11: downloaded; sha256 equals the GitHub release asset digest (sha256:a04154a0…). rizin.exe reports 'rizin 0.9.1'; Cutter v2.5.0's rizin submodule is c3a90e92 (= rizin v0.9.1). pdg verified on fixtures/pecli with ghidra.sleighhome set.

previous.name: rizin-windows-static-v0.9.1.zip
previous.why_replaced: no rz-ghidra: no decompilation on Windows

artifact.name: dotnet-runtime-8.0.31-win-x64.zip
artifact.hash_provenance: 2026-10-06 on Windows 11 (interactive host): downloaded from builds.dotnet.microsoft.com; SHA-512 matched the official value in https://builds.dotnet.microsoft.com/dotnet/release-metadata/8.0/releases.json (release 8.0.31, file dotnet-runtime-win-x64.zip); sha256 computed locally from the same verified bytes.

temurin-jre.role: Optional: Java runtime for CFR and jadx (Java/Android code recovery). Eclipse Temurin 17 JRE, installed side by side under tools\jre like the .NET runtime; no machine-wide install. Without it the app falls back to a JDK/JRE 8+ already on PATH/JAVA_HOME.

artifact.name: OpenJDK17U-jre_x64_windows_hotspot_17.0.20.1_1.zip
artifact.hash_provenance: 2026-10-06 on Windows 11 (interactive host): downloaded from the Adoptium GitHub release; sha256 computed locally and matched the official value in OpenJDK17U-jre_x64_windows_hotspot_17.0.20.1_1.zip.sha256.txt published next to the asset (and the 'checksum' field of the Adoptium v3 assets API response).

cfr.role: Optional: Java bytecode decompiler for .jar/.class (CFR, MIT). Single jar run as `java -jar` in a separate process; needs the JRE above (or any Java 8+).

artifact.name: cfr-0.152.jar
artifact.hash_provenance: 2026-10-06 on Windows 11 (interactive host): downloaded the release asset with curl; sha256 computed locally. The release publishes no checksum file, so the pin is trust-on-first-use of the GitHub release asset at tag 0.152; a clean decompile of fixtures/javacli with this exact jar is recorded in tests/test_jvm.py.

jadx.role: Optional: Android recovery (jadx CLI, Apache-2.0): APK/DEX/AAB to Java-like sources plus decoded resources. Run as `java -cp lib/jadx-1.5.6-all.jar jadx.cli.JadxCLI` in a separate process; needs Java 11+ (the JRE above).

artifact.name: jadx-1.5.6.zip
artifact.hash_provenance: 2026-10-06 on Windows 11 (interactive host): downloaded the release asset with curl; sha256 computed locally and matched the asset digest published by the GitHub releases API (sha256:545ea2be...8974).

rust.role: Rust compiler for building rebuilt programs as Windows .exe files (cargo + rustc, stable 1.97.0, host/target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu). Installed privately under tools\rust by the official rustup-init 1.29.1 (sha256-pinned below) run as a lock-declared post_install step with RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME inside the tools folder: no administrator rights, no PATH changes, no Visual Studio Build Tools (the GNU toolchain ships its own self-contained mingw linker). Without it the app falls back to a cargo already on PATH.
rust.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (rustup, Rust toolchain); the bundled mingw-w64 linker files carry their own permissive/GPL-with-exception licenses

artifact.name: rustup-init.exe
artifact.hash_provenance: 2026-10-06 on Windows 11: downloaded rustup-init.exe 1.29.1 (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc host binary, which only needs the Windows system DLLs) from static.rust-lang.org; sha256 computed locally and matched the official value in rustup-init.exe.sha256 published next to it (https://static.rust-lang.org/rustup/archive/1.29.1/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/rustup-init.exe.sha256). 1.29.1 is the version named in https://static.rust-lang.org/rustup/release-stable.toml that day.

footprint.note: rustup-init (12.7 MB, pinned above) downloads the toolchain components itself (about 147 MB) and unpacks to about 840 MB. rustup verifies every component's hash against Rust's signed release manifests (channel-rust-1.97.0.toml); that check is rustup's, the lock pins only the installer and the toolchain version.

webview2_evergreen_bootstrapper.role: Required by Tauri on Windows. Evergreen runtime is NOT bundled; Install-RebuildStudio.ps1 checks for it and downloads the small bootstrapper if absent.
webview2_evergreen_bootstrapper.hash_note: Microsoft re-publishes this bootstrapper under a stable URL, so the hash changes; instead of a hash the installer REQUIRES a valid Authenticode signature from 'Microsoft Corporation' (Get-AuthenticodeSignature) before running it.

vc_redist_x64.role: Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 x64 runtime (needed by the Rust MSVC binary, PyInstaller bundle, rizin MSVC build). Detected only; Doctor prints the download link, nothing is bundled.

rust.note: CI uses the stable channel; the pin records the version the shell was validated with (cargo check on Linux). Windows MSVC builds are unverified until docs/WINDOWS_RELEASE_GATES.md gate W1 passes.
rust.private_install: Guided setup (tool 'rust') installs 1.97.0 for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu privately; the Rust builder prefers it over PATH. Release builds of the shell itself still use the msvc target above.

python.note: CI (windows.yml, linux.yml) and the PyInstaller sidecar build use 3.12. The Linux dev host that wrote the controller ran 3.13.16; both are exercised by linux.yml's pytest matrix. 3.11 is the declared floor in controller/pyproject.toml but is not exercised.

sbom_tools.pin_file: scripts/windows/requirements-build.txt (pip-licenses, cyclonedx-bom); cargo-cyclonedx is installed with `cargo install cargo-cyclonedx --version 0.5.9 --locked`

sidecar_build.also_built: rebuild-mcp.exe from scripts/windows/mcp_entry.py (shipped under runtime\Scripts for Install-Clients.ps1)
